_README: Battery testing workflow — Instrumentation spec §5. Every step carries purpose, controlled and measured parameters, expected result, considerations, common mistakes, safety and data output. DRAFT — review before treating as procedure. This is a teaching outline, NOT a laboratory SOP: your group's own written procedure always takes precedence.

items.name: Cell assembly
items.purpose: Build the cell so that every later measurement is about the material rather than about how the cell was put together.
items.expected: A sealed cell with even contact pressure, full separator coverage and sufficient electrolyte.
considerations: Record the active material mass NOW, independently of the instrument. This is the number every gravimetric result depends on.
Keep the assembly sequence identical between cells — crimping pressure, spacer choice and spring orientation all affect reproducibility.
Make the separator overhang the electrode on all sides.
mistakes: Not recording the mass, or recording it only on the instrument where it cannot be checked later
Varying assembly details between cells and then attributing the scatter to the material
Too little electrolyte for the electrode's porosity
safety: Assemble air- and moisture-sensitive chemistries in an appropriate controlled atmosphere. Follow your group's written procedure, not this outline.
items.dataOutput: None yet — but the mass recorded here propagates into every result that follows.

items.name: Inspection
items.purpose: Catch a bad cell before spending days of channel time on it.
items.expected: No deformation, no leakage, an open-circuit voltage in a plausible range for the chemistry and assembled state.
considerations: A freshly built cell has a characteristic starting voltage range for its chemistry. A value far outside it usually means a short or a mis-assembly.
Check the crimp or seal visually before connecting anything.
mistakes: Skipping inspection and discovering the fault a week into a cycling run
Ignoring a voltage reading that does not make sense
safety: Do not put a deformed, swollen or leaking cell on test. Isolate it and follow your group's disposal procedure.
items.dataOutput: A recorded initial voltage and condition note.

items.name: Connection
items.purpose: Connect the cell to the channel so that what the instrument measures is the cell and not the wiring.
items.expected: Firm, correct-polarity contact, with sense leads at the cell terminals where four-wire sensing is available.
considerations: Confirm polarity before starting. Reversed connection can damage a cell and in some chemistries is hazardous.
Where the channel supports four-wire sensing, use it and check where the sense leads actually attach.
Record which channel each cell is on, next to its mass.
mistakes: Reversed polarity
Two-wire sensing used without realising, so lead resistance is measured as cell resistance
Cell connected to a different channel than the schedule was assigned to
safety: Verify polarity before applying any current.

items.name: Rest
items.purpose: Let the cell wet fully and settle before anything is imposed on it.
items.expected: Voltage drift slowing to a small, decreasing rate.
considerations: Judge readiness by the drift RATE, not by elapsed time. Slow drift and true equilibrium look identical over a short window.
Porous electrodes and viscous electrolytes may need considerably longer than expected.
mistakes: Using a fixed rest time regardless of whether the cell settled
Starting the schedule while the cell is still wetting
items.dataOutput: Voltage vs time — the baseline every later measurement is referenced to.

items.name: OCV measurement
items.purpose: Record the settled open-circuit voltage and confirm the cell is healthy enough to test.
items.expected: A stable value consistent with the chemistry and assembled state.
considerations: A voltage that continues to slide at a constant rate suggests self-discharge or a soft short rather than slow equilibration.
Record the value — it is the reference point for interpreting everything that follows.
mistakes: Treating a still-drifting value as the equilibrium voltage
Not recording it at all
safety: A cell whose voltage is falling steadily should be investigated before current is applied.
items.dataOutput: Settled OCV and the drift rate at the end of the rest.

items.name: Formation
items.purpose: Allow interfacial layers to form under controlled, low-rate conditions before the study proper begins.
items.expected: First-cycle coulombic efficiency below later cycles, then efficiency settling.
considerations: Stop when coulombic efficiency has stabilised, not after a fixed number of cycles.
Formation cycles must never be pooled with steady-state cycles when reporting efficiency or capacity.
mistakes: Reporting first-cycle efficiency as characteristic of the material
Starting a rate study before formation has settled
items.dataOutput: First-cycle irreversible capacity; coulombic efficiency per formation cycle.

items.name: Charge
items.purpose: Add charge at a defined rate up to the upper voltage limit.
items.expected: Voltage rising to the upper limit; the step ending on that limit rather than on its time limit.
considerations: Take the voltage limits from the chemistry and electrolyte stability, never from another system's protocol.
Sample finely enough to resolve the IR step at the current change.
mistakes: Copying a voltage window from a different chemistry
Calculating capacity from the programmed rather than the recorded current
safety: Set voltage, current, capacity, time and temperature limits on every step. A step with no time limit can run indefinitely.
items.dataOutput: Charge capacity; the charge branch of the V–Q curve.

items.name: CV hold (if applicable)
items.purpose: Hold at the upper voltage and let the current decay to a defined cutoff, giving a reproducible fully-charged state.
items.expected: Current decaying monotonically below the termination threshold.
considerations: The termination current sets how full the cell ends up — report it with any capacity derived from it.
Always set a time limit: a high-impedance cell may never reach the cutoff.
mistakes: Omitting the time limit
Comparing CC-CV capacity with CC-only capacity
Changing the cutoff partway through a study
items.dataOutput: Additional charge during the hold; the CC/CV capacity split.

items.name: Rest
items.purpose: Let the cell relax between charge and discharge so the next step starts from a defined state.
items.expected: Voltage relaxing towards a quasi-equilibrium value.
considerations: The relaxation shape itself carries information about internal transport.
Keep the rest duration identical across cycles being compared.
mistakes: Varying rest duration between cycles and then comparing them

items.name: Discharge
items.purpose: Remove charge at a defined rate down to the lower voltage limit — the step most results are calculated from.
items.expected: Voltage falling to the lower limit, with an IR step at the current reversal.
considerations: The discharge branch is where specific capacity, capacitance and IR drop are normally read.
Decide explicitly whether the IR drop is inside or outside ΔV, and state it.
mistakes: Not stating the IR convention
Using total electrode mass in one calculation and active mass in another
safety: Do not discharge below the lower limit to extract more capacity.
items.dataOutput: Discharge capacity; the discharge branch; IR drop; coulombic efficiency when paired with the charge step.

items.name: Rest
items.purpose: Relax before the next cycle begins.
items.expected: Voltage recovering towards a quasi-equilibrium value.
considerations: Recovery that shrinks over cycle life can indicate rising impedance.
mistakes: Omitting the rest so each cycle starts from a different state

items.name: Repeat
items.purpose: Loop the cycle block for as many cycles as the question requires.
items.measured: voltage, capacity and efficiency per cycle
items.expected: Per-cycle capacity and coulombic efficiency, tracked over the full run.
considerations: Keep every parameter fixed across the loop. Changing the rate mid-study makes the retention curve uninterpretable.
Check the step end-reason periodically rather than only at the end.
mistakes: Normalising retention to cycle 1, which is dominated by formation
Changing protocol partway and comparing across the change
safety: Check the cell periodically during long runs. Swelling, heating or leakage means stopping the test, not waiting for it to finish.
items.dataOutput: Capacity retention; coulombic efficiency vs cycle number; the full cycling dataset.
